identity: scon_<12 hex>, keyed on session and creation ordinal; edits keep the ID
revision: 1-based append-only history; references MUST include session_id, constellation_id and revision
migration: Optional independently versioned extension on session v1/v2. No read-time database migration. Absent means not recorded, never no coherent thought.
graph_pin: Existing inquiry_interaction.graph_hash plus graph_id, graph schema, inquiry_id, session revision and checkpoint; a changed hash is stale and is never rebound on read.
source_spans: Half-open Unicode code point offsets into the exact stored prompt or reading block. Server verifies origin, source identity, exact text and source SHA-256. No source-unit ID is minted before compilation.
limits: Semantic session object, not a Differential constellation Ground or perceptual artifact.
The organising question is human-authored or human-confirmed; no added model pass.
A model reading block can be anchored only after it exists.
Captures or content edits after compiler entry are retrospective. Earlier captures remain in history.
Shared ancestry proposes structural membership only; no lexical similarity or invented relation.
All candidate IDs and the full count survive overflow. Human confirmation is limited to eight claims; narrowing is explicit.
Membership, judgment and graph evidence status are independent. No human review edits model claims.
Perceptual questions are non-executable. Recognition is interpretation; chromatic/flow claims remain capability gaps.
concurrency: Every human write requires expected_checkpoint; revision writes also require expected_constellation_revision. Human writes increment checkpoint. Driver terminal writes preserve the latest human-owned extension under CAS and lease checks.
downstream: C/D consume a pinned history revision, anchors/authorship, organising question, alternatives, inspection.graph, candidate versus confirmed refs, missing_links, limits and judgment. Never infer human ratification from reference coverage or a successful request.
